resources.string: This solver uses simplified mechanical models and the principle of energy conservation to estimate webbing stretch and maximum sag following a mainline failure.
The results are theoretical estimates, not experimentally verified predictions.
Real-world behavior can differ significantly due to dynamic effects, friction, material variability, connection behavior and other mechanisms not fully represented in the model.
Conservation of energy provides a maximum-deflection estimate within the assumptions of the implemented model. It does not guarantee an absolute upper bound for sag or forces in a real failure event.
This software does not guarantee that a highline setup is safe and must not be used as the sole basis for rigging or safety decisions.
Highlining involves serious risks of injury or death.
By selecting Accept and Continue, the user acknowledges these limitations.
